title: The Clockwork Bird
text: A brass bird flits from beam to beam in the ruined forge, singing a song from the forge's best days, when the furnaces roared and the smiths were proud. Its wings click as it flies. Each note is a little lower than the last; it is running down.

options.label: The cleverest hands wind it up again, so that its song may go on.

outcomes.text: It sings brighter than before, then leads you through the ruins to its maker's room, where it has long been waiting to go.

options.label: Catch it for the House. A thing so fine should not be left to rust.

outcomes.text: It is a fine toy worth a good deal, though it never stops trying to escape.
Its brass beak is sharp. It goes for the eyes, fighting hard against the hand that holds it.

options.label: Let it run down. Its maker is long gone, and so are its best days.

outcomes.text: The song slows, then stops mid-note. The forge is very quiet, and very dead.
